title: Lineage VI foundational body plan
scope: Foundational body plan of Lineage VI, the segmented exoskeletal radiation, including skeletal growth mode as a branch-level axis and its ancestral state; usable within shared-setting ecology and adopted downstream story development.
claims: Lineage VI has a segmented body enclosed in a jointed external skeleton, with segment counts and regional specialisation varying by branch.
The lineage is the planet's most species-rich macroscopic animal radiation, and most members are small-bodied.
Some branches fly; their flight is small-scale and arose independently of the flight evolved in Lineages I and III.
The lineage supplies pollinator-analogue, litter and soil, parasitic, scavenging, predatory, and swarm-prey roles.
Skeletal growth mode varies by branch across three modes.
Moult branches shed the whole skeleton periodically, pass through a soft vulnerable phase, may undergo life-stage transformation, and remain small.
Seam-growth branches never shed; their skeletons expand continuously at flexible inter-plate seams, without a soft phase and without life-stage transformation.
Rolling-replacement branches shed and regrow plates individually and are never wholly soft.
Whole-body moulting is the ancestral condition; rolling replacement and seam growth are derived escapes from its soft phase and size ceiling.
Freed from the moult constraint, seam-growth branches include the lineage's large-bodied members, which exceed the sizes Earth arthropods reach.
boundaries: Plate, seam, moult branch, seam-growth branch, and rolling-replacement branch are author-facing functional descriptions, not in-world names or formal taxonomy.
The plan establishes no insect, crustacean, arachnid, myriapod, or other Earth-clade homology; exoskeleton describes an external jointed skeleton only.
Species, names, segment counts, limb counts, sizes, proportions, colours, lifespans, and the branch inventory remain open.
Skeleton composition, chemistry, seam mechanics, moult mechanics, hardening, repair, damage tolerance, and mineral requirements remain open.

Most members are small-bodied and exceed the sizes Earth arthropods reach are qualitative; no measurement, size range, upper limit, or comparison figure is established, and no particular large animal is established as existing.

Larger-than-Earth body sizes require respiratory, circulatory, and structural support that this record does not supply; the mechanism remains open and binding, and large branches are not exempt from physical or physiological limits.

Life-stage transformation is available to moult branches only as a possibility; its extent, forms, triggers, and whether any branch uses it remain open, and seam-growth and rolling-replacement branches do not use it.
The three modes describe growth strategy only; they establish no fixed branch count, no exclusive niche assignment, and no rule that any niche belongs to one mode.
Ancestral moulting is an evolutionary-history claim establishing no timeline, transitional form, or surviving ancestral species.
Flight in this lineage is small-scale at the lineage level; whether any large branch is flight-capable remains open, as do wing structure, origin, and performance.

The lineage's scavenging and litter roles sit alongside the thread decomposers of canon://world/shared-universe-001/ecology/thread-decomposer-foundational-body-architecture, which remain the primary macroscopic recycler kingdom.

No Lineage VI branch is established as present, abundant, or absent at any particular location, including the initial basin, and no branch is identified with any pest, pollinator, parasite, or mythic creature.
Reproduction, egg or brood form, development, sociality, swarming, communication, senses, internal anatomy, disease, and predator-prey relationships remain open.

Mana patterns remain open; no Mana organ, specialised ability, System progression, universal creature level, spawn mechanism, reward, Skill, trait payload, or Ancestry Development rule is established.
Earth life of any era and mythological creatures may inspire author-facing design; no living, extinct, or legendary Earth species is transplanted directly.
Food, energy, minerals, oxygen, reproduction, disease, injury, mortality, and carrying capacity remain binding ecological constraints.
story_implications: Everyday small life can fill background description from this lineage without every organism being spectacular.
Moult branches can be caught in their soft vulnerable phase, and seamed bodies can be damaged at their weak points.
Rare large forms exceeding Earth arthropod scale are biologically available through seam-growth branches.
Every species, size, local presence, and encounter requires its own evidence and records.
system_implications: The body plan describes ordinary planetary ecology under CAL0 WLD1.2D and WLD2.1A+D.
No System mechanic, creature progression rule, spawn source, reward, or specialised Mana ability is established.
research_questions: What skeleton composition and seam or moult mechanics implement each growth mode?
What respiratory, circulatory, and structural support permits larger-than-Earth body sizes, and what upper limits follow?
Which branches exist in each growth mode, and which niches do they occupy?
Do any moult branches use life-stage transformation, and in what forms?
How does small-scale flight arise in this lineage, and is any large branch flight-capable?
How do the lineage's scavenging roles divide labour with the thread decomposers?
sources: Author structural direction and selection on 2026-08-17

author_approval.evidence: After the growth-mode cards were presented, the Author directed that all three modes be retained as branches and that some members exceed Earth arthropod sizes; the revised three-branch model was presented with an ancestry question, and the Author selected 'A — Moult ancestral' on 2026-08-17.
